articleTitle: Compact, low-power, photonic macrochip-based computing systems
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We review progress in efficient silicon photonic interconnects. In particular, we discuss opportunities and challenges of compact, low-power, photonic macrochip-based computing systems enabled by WDM silicon photonic link technology with high bandwidth-density-distance product.

articleTitle: Experimental realization of photonic synthetic matters on-a-chip
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We show nanoscale optical engineering in the complex dielectric permittivity plane to realize photonic synthetic matters on-a-chip, by which unidirectional reflectionless light propagation and asymmetric mode conversion have been experimentally demonstrated at the exceptional point.

articleTitle: Looking inside a fiber: Measuring mode content & properties
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We describe classification schemes for distinguishing eigenmodes in fibers, and highlight their similarities and differences. We then describe characterization schemes useful for elucidating their properties, such as field and polarization distributions, dispersion, and nonlinear impairments - characteristics of interest for fibers being developed for MDM.

articleTitle: Optical interconnects for advanced memory modules: From disaggregated racks to full datacenter computers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: This talk will layout a vision for flexible datacenter deployments using optically interconnected modules, taking the approach that datacenter-scale applications could benefit from a more tightly coupled environment.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of crosstalk accumulation in a ring-core fiber
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We investigate the crosstalk accumulation between mode-groups of a ring-core fiber for lengths of 15 m, 200 m and 2 km and observe the discrete modes become fully coupled.

articleTitle: Integrated optical connection module for 7-core multi-core fiber and 7 single mode fibers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: An integrated optical connection module was developed that connects 7-core multi-core fiber and 7 single mode fibers. Insertion loss below 0.5 dB, PDL below 0.1dB and crosstalk better than -50 dB were realized.

articleTitle: Pitch Reducing Optical Fiber Array and multicore fiber for space-division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: The “vanishing core” concept in conjunction with a highly uniform 7-core fiber makes possible a monolithic, low-loss, low crosstalk, independently addressable, multicore fiber link in an all-glass, spliceable fanout for MC fiber.

articleTitle: Remotely pumped multicore erbium-doped fiber amplifier system with high pumping efficiency
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We have experimentally clarified the optical amplification characteristics of a remotely pumped multicore erbium-doped fiber amplifier system. The pumping efficiencies of the system are ~4 times higher than those of the distributed Raman amplification system.

articleTitle: SDN control for hybrid OCS/electrical datacenter networks: An enabler or just a convenience?
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: A new SDN control plane architecture for hybrid optical/electrical switch networks is demonstrated. Compared to traditional VLAN-based control, our OpenFlow implementation is more scalable and enables faster reconfiguration of multihop or multipath networks.

articleTitle: Linearly polarized mode division multiplexed transmission over ring-index multimode fibres
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: LP modes in ring-index multimode fibres (RI-MMFs) are proposed to carry parallel-data for spatial multiplexing systems with low-complexity MIMO processing. Simulation shows that, with 3×3MIMO, 6×20Gb/s NRZ error-free transmission is achieved over 1km-RI-MMFs using IMDD.

articleTitle: Future datacenter interfaces based on existing and emerging optics technologies
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Mainstream datacenter interfaces use NRZ modulation, VCSEL or DFB lasers, parallel or WDM channels, packaged in pluggable modules. Emerging technologies are higher order modulation, faster lane rate, InP or Si modulator (Si Mod), and board mounted optics. Future datacenter interfaces will use all of these to increase link rates.

articleTitle: SDM-WDM hybrid reconfigurable add-drop nodes for self-homodyne photonic networks
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We present an SDM-WDM hybrid add-drop network node compatible with SDM-based self-homodyne transmission. OSNR penalties were less than 0.7 dB, but net spectral efficiency was slightly sacrificed.

articleTitle: Photonic lantern spatial multiplexers in space-division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Photonic-lanterns are lossless spatial-multiplexers that scramble N signals onto the N modes of a multi-mode fiber without mode- dependent loss. They can scale to large N and have enabled transmission over a fiber supporting 12 spatial and polarization-modes.

articleTitle: Low-loss fusion splice technique for multicore fiber with a large cladding diameter
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Fusion splice technique for multicore fiber was demonstrated. Low splice loss less than 0.1 dB in average was realized by using end-view alignment system and swing electrode system under small cleaved angle condition.

articleTitle: 210Tb/s self-homodyne PDM-WDM-SDM transmission with DFB lasers in a 19-core fiber
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We demonstrate a 210Tb/s self-homodyne transmission system based on a 19-core using DFB laser transmitters and compare the transmission penalties for self-homodyne and intradyne detection in single and dual polarization schemes.

articleTitle: Multicore fiber with ring structure
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: The characteristics of MCFs with one-ring structure are reviewed. The MCFs realize the number of cores larger than 10, suppressed crosstalk and enlarged A<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> under limited cladding diameter in terms of mechanical reliability.

articleTitle: Low-loss all-optical quantum switching
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We present a two-input, two-output, single-photon switch prototype that is capable of achieving insertion loss <; 0.6 dB and switching speed > 5 GHz.

articleTitle: Few-mode fibers for mode-division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: The design of few-mode fibers will be discussed from the point of view of key attributes and fundamental limitations. We will consider the maximum number of modes that might be supported in a practical fiber.

articleTitle: Converting a multimode fiber into a single-mode fiber
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: A multimode fiber infrastructure can be used to support single-mode Silicon Photonics by coupling only to the lowest-order mode of the fiber. This allows Silicon Photonics to share a common fiber infrastructure with multimode VCSELs.

articleTitle: Towards widespread SDN adoption: Need for synergy between photonics and SDN within the data center
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: This paper looks at the use of photonics in future data center networks and stresses the need for SDN Controller and concepts - programmability, virtualization and end-to-end optimization - to control, manage and automate these elements to enable an optimized, elastic and agile data center.

articleTitle: Experimental frequency-domain channel matrix characterization for SDM-MIMO-OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We present the first experimental frequency-domain channel matrix characterization for optical SDM-MIMO-OFDM systems. Data from 6×6 WDM-SDM transmission over 10×50km few mode fiber confirm non-unitary channel behavior, including 18dB frequency-averaged MDL and spatially-correlated Gaussian noise.

articleTitle: Silicon photonic interconnection networks for data centers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: To improve data center performance we seek to increase bandwidth and reduce power consumption. Integrated silicon photonics can help achieve both. System level simulations are required to demonstrate network level performance advantages (latency, execution time).

articleTitle: Design strategy of uncoupled multicore fiber enabling high spatial capacity transmission
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: The relationships between fiber parameters and spatial capacity of uncoupled multicore fiber are investigated theoretically. Preferable fiber design and characteristics enabling high spatial capacity transmission is proposed.

articleTitle: Degenerate mode-group division multiplexing using MIMO digital signal processing
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: MIMO DSP is employed to improve the performance of degenerate mode-group division multiplexing in 8 km of conventional GI-MMF. Compensation of the mode coupling, induced by the launch and propagation, between and inside each degenerate mode-group is investigated in order to reduce the DSP complexity.

articleTitle: Connection characteristics of MU-type multicore fiber connector
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We have developed a 7-core-fiber connector. We employed Oldham's coupling mechanism inside the MU-type connector plug housing and realized an average attenuation of 0.13 dB and good repeatability for mating cycles.

articleTitle: REACToR: A reconfigurable packet and circuit ToR switch
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We are designing REACToR, a hybrid ToR that enables scalable, high-speed networks by pairing optical circuit switching with comparatively underprovisioned packet switching. The key insight driving our work is that by moving the vast majority-but not all-of the buffering out of the switch and into end hosts, more scalable, lower-cost interconnect fabrics can be supported.

articleTitle: Large effective area FMF with low DMGD
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We present few mode fiber designs for mode division multiplexing applications. We discuss key fiber design considerations and show profiles designs and actual fiber examples to achieve large effective area and low DMGD.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of CSI estimation techniques for FMF transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Channel state information (CSI) of transmission systems is important for mode dependent loss (MDL) estimation. Using the heuristic minimum mean square error method, we show MDL estimation within 0.3dB with respect to the least-squares method.

articleTitle: DMT modulation for enabling low-power unretimed high-speed optical modules
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We present Monte-Carlo simulation results demonstrating feasibility of unretimed serial 56 Gb/s host ASIC-to-ASIC transmission based on DMT modulation. The model includes a 6 bit DAC/ADC, CEI-28G-VSR electrical channel, and 25G-class DFB transmitter.

articleTitle: Measurement of structural irregularity dependence on mode coupling along multi-core fiber using multi-channel OTDR system
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We have successfully measured the structural irregularity dependence on mode coupling along a multi-core fiber by using a multi-channel OTDR system. The system has a high dynamic range of more than 60 dB and a high spatial resolution of 10 m.

articleTitle: Optoacoustic isolators in photonic crystal fibre
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Coherent optically-driven GHz acoustic waves, tightly guided in the micron-sized core of photonic crystal fibre, enable reconfigurable dynamic optical isolation and switching, providing new functionality that is useful in various types of all-optical fibre systems.

articleTitle: Photonic integration technologies for high efficiency WDM transceivers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We describe the design of high efficiency EML and DFB-MZ chips and present performance characteristics of small footprint low power consumption 10 Gb/s and 100Gb/s TOSAs built leveraging InP monolithic and hybrid integration.

articleTitle: Long-distance and high-capacity transmission with multicore fiber
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Space-division-multiplexing is an attractive approach to increase the capacity of submarine cable systems. The feasibility of transoceanic class transmission with multicore fiber was confirmed in 7 × 40 × 128 Gbit/s transmission over 6160 km.

articleTitle: Vitalizing data-center networks using OpenFlow
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We address network virtualization in datacenter using OpenFlow to improve security and performance isolation among tenants. We present our solutions and open source implementations for both hop-by-hop and overlay schemes, and their integration with OpenStack/Quantum.

articleTitle: High quality InGaP micropillars directly grown on silicon
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: High quality lattice-mismatched micron-sized InGaP pillars directly grown on silicon are studied using time-resolved photoluminescence. Micropillars with single-crystalline wurtzite phase exhibit bright photoluminescence and very long lifetimes, promising for optoelectronic devices and solar cell applications.

articleTitle: Temporal variations in the channel matrix in few-mode fiber recirculating loop transmission
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We study short-term variations and long-term stability of the channel matrix for a few-mode fiber re-circulating loop using a few-mode EDFA for inline amplification. Our results are based on the singular values of the channel matrix and the system performance per mode.

articleTitle: Experimental evaluation of the reduction of the received signal penalty due to inter-core crosstalk in a lossy 7-core Multicore Fiber by using bidirectional signal assignment
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We experimentally evaluated and confirmed the effectiveness of bidirectional signal assignment for reducing the inter-core XT induced penalties with a lossy 7-core, 43-km MCF having 21 splicing connections.

articleTitle: Physical layer encryption by Y-00 protocol for secure optical interconnection between data centers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Physical layer encryption by Y-00 protocol is proposed for secure interconnection of data centers. 25-Gb/s, 120-km Y-00 signal transmission is successfully demonstrated with wavelength division multiplexing (10 ch × 2.5 Gb/s, 50-GHz channel spacing).

articleTitle: Attojoule optoelectronics - Why and how
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Optical interconnect requirements have driven optoelectronic device energies into the low femtojoule range. With integrated optical and electronic nanostructures, we could continue deeply into the attojoule range, with significant potential impact for systems.

articleTitle: Phase-regeneration of 2ASK-BPSK in a one-mode phase-sensitive amplifier
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We demonstrate the regeneration of 2ASK-BPSK in a phase-sensitive amplifier. Its regeneration ability is investigated for different degrees of imposed phase noise by complex-field analysis.

articleTitle: Quantum-dot physics for applications in semiconductor lasers and quantum optics
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: This talk discusses theory developments for describing changes in many-body carrier-interaction processes arising from 3-dimensional quantum confinement. The improvements are necessary for investigating quantum-dot-laser performance at underlying-physics level and developing non-classical-light sources for quantum-information technologies.

articleTitle: An ultra-short InP nanowire laser monolithic integrated on (001) silicon substrate
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Silicon photonics holds the promise of converging electronics and photonics. The key component, a low-cost high-performance laser, is still missing however within this platform. Although novel solutions have been proposed to increase the light emission directly from silicon (or Ge), compared with their III-V counterparts, these solutions are still in their infancy. Recently, the epitaxial growth of III-Vs on silicon regained a wide interest. III-V nanowire growth has been widely investigated. However, most of the III-V nanowire lasers on silicon require a complex cleaving and transfer process, which make these devices not suitable for dense integration. In addition, the large cavity dimensions along the nanowire axis (several microns) hinder dense integration. Here, we present the first room-temperature operation of an ultra-short InP nanowire laser that is epitaxially grown on an exactly [001] oriented silicon substrate. The sub-micron sized laser cavity largely enhances the interaction of the lasing mode with the gain medium, and a large spontaneous emission factor has been obtained.

articleTitle: Optimization of compact photonic crystal cavity using the gentle confinement method
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We demonstrate that the gentle confinement method is effective for optimizing area-limited photonic crystal cavities. We also show the importance of the boundary and that optimal boundary parameters improves the Q-factor significantly.

articleTitle: Integrated optical circulators and isolators on a ultra-low-loss silicon nitride platform
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We show our progress on ring-based optical isolators and circulators, designed on both silica and silicon based photonic integration platforms. Isolation levels of better than −20 dB have been shown theoretically and −9 dB experimentally.

articleTitle: Recent progress in space-division multiplexing R&D in Japan
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Space-division multiplexing (SDM) via multicore/multimode fibers is currently being actively explored to overcome the capacity limit of single-mode fiber. In this paper, recent progress in R&D on SDM in Japan will be introduced.

articleTitle: Mode multiplexing, characterization and processing using a Spatial Light Modulator
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: In this talk the applications and associated techniques of Spatial Light Modulators for MDM research will be discussed. Including modal decomposition, (de)multiplexing and routing as well as features of practical importance such as aberration correction.

articleTitle: Enabling energy efficient exascale computing applications with optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: The past few years has seen a sea change in computer architecture that will impact every facet of our society as every electronic device from cell phone to supercomputer will need to confront parallelism of unprecedented scale. Enabling future advances in sustained computational performance will require fundamental advances in computer architecture and programming models that are nothing short of reinventing computing. Photonic interconnect technologies will play an essential role to enable future progress in exascale computing.

articleTitle: Multicore erbium doped fiber amplifier with 5 THz bandwidth, high-gain and low NF
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Core-pumped 7-core EDFA with two stage amplification is realized. Combination of its higher gain and GFF enables wide bandwidth operation. NF of Less than 5.5 dB is achieved with improved fan-in device.

articleTitle: A monolithic optical front-end for soft-decision error correction decoders
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We investigate a monolithic optical front-end for soft-decision low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoders based on 100 Gb/s polarization division multiplexed quadrature shift keying (PM-QPSK) coherent detection.

articleTitle: Splice induced performance penalty in mode multiplexed few-mode fibers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We show that splice-induced discrete mode coupling leads to performance penalties in mode-multiplexed transmission systems. This can be explained by an increased waveform variance and nonlinear induced changes of the coupling characteristics.

articleTitle: Green photonics for data and computer communication
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Record low dissipated energy of 118 to 56 fJ/bit is reported for our VCSELs operating error-free at 40, 30, and 25 Gb/s across 50, 500, and 1000 m of MMF, respectively.

articleTitle: Recent progress in photonic crystals and their applications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: I will report on the recent progresses in 2D and 3D photonic crystals, including 2D high-Q nanocavities-based new phenomena, novel lasers including ultra-compact Si Raman lasers, thermal emission control, and on-demand 3D optical guiding, etc.

articleTitle: Long-distance mode-division multiplexed transmission using normalized adaptive frequency-domain equalization
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We investigate normalized adaptive frequency-domain equalization (NA-FDE) in a 1,000-km mode-division multiplexed (MDM) transmission experiment. We show that master-slave phase estimation can be used to reduce carrier recovery complexity with less than 1 dB Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-penalty.

articleTitle: Idler chirp optimization in a pulse-pumped parametric amplifier
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: A simple engineering rule for idler characteristic optimization in pulsed fiber optic parametric amplifiers operated in transparency is derived. The theoretical results are validated in both simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: A long-lived solid-state quantum memory
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: A necessary part of a quantum repeater is an on-demand quantum memory. In this paper we report on recent progress of achieving such a memory in a solid-state system. We show storage of a few photon optical pulse as a spin-wave in a crystal, preserving the states' coherence. We show how it is possible to extend the storage time and increase the process efficiency.

articleTitle: Preliminary results of the first optical Quantum Communication in Mexico: 2 photons / bit at 5 Mbps using 62 and 125 Km in a commercial optical network
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We implement a QPSK optical quantum near-homodyne scheme up to 125 Km in a commercial photonics network using two narrow independent lasers with coherent states, 2 photons/bit and 5 Mbps transmission rate.

articleTitle: On-chip nonreciprocal photonic devices using magneto-optical oxide thin films
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We report a monolithically integrated optical isolator on silicon using polycrystalline CeYIG thin films. An isolation ratio of 19.5±2.9 dB was demonstrated at 1541 nm.

articleTitle: Unleashing the spatial domain in optical fiber communications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: SDM offers the potential for ultrahigh information-flux optical communications at petabit/s level capacities, and also reduced costs per-bit. I review progress to date and discuss some of the technological/commercial challenges and opportunities that lie ahead.

articleTitle: Self correcting quantum random number generators using tapered amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We present a new implementation of a quantum random number generator that consists of tapered amplifier optical semiconductor devices and an array of random number registration techniques, including quantum feedback/forward control for removing bias.

articleTitle: High-speed, high-temperature VCSELs for optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Directly modulated VCSELs operating at 40Gb/s are required for next generation optical interconnect standards. Using a refined high-speed design we demonstrate GaAs-based VCSELs that operate error-free at 47Gb/s at 25°C, and 40Gb/s at 85°C.

articleTitle: Multicore erbium doped fiber amplifier for space division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: MC-EDFA is expected as one of the key component for SDM systems. Its possibilities and abilities to enable high-capacity, low power consumption and cost reduction are summarized. Also, recent reports utilizing MC-EDFA are introduced.

articleTitle: Multi-Tb/s data transport system for the square kilometre array radio telescope
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: In about four years the construction of the world's largest radio telescope, the SKA, will start. This paper describes the initial SKA design and the approach in the development of its multi-Tb/s data transport system.

articleTitle: Adaptive control of mode-dependent gain in multi-mode erbium-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We demonstrate adaptive control of mode-dependent gain in a multi-mode erbium-doped fiber amplifier by placing a spatial light modulator in line with the pump laser.

articleTitle: A 30 GHz silicon photonic platform: Multi-project wafer shuttles for next-generation optical systems
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Shared shuttle run services are ideal for rapid and relatively inexpensive prototyping. We present a silicon photonic platform that offers monolithically integrated modulators and photodetectors with 30 GHz bandwidths, available through the OpSIS MPW service.

articleTitle: Continuous-variable QKD with post-selection is secure
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Post-selection is a standard part of discrete variable QKD protocols, however attempts to prove security when post-selection is deployed in continuous variable QKD protocols have until now been limited. Here, by using a carefully tailored post-selection protocol, we prove unconditional security and show that significant performance improvements are achieved.

articleTitle: Electrically driven photonic-crystal lasers using an ultra-compact embedded active region
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We have successfully developed an electrically driven photonic-crystal nanocavity laser. Thanks to the development of an ultra-compact embedded active-region structure, a record low threshold current and energy needed for transferring a single bit are achieved.

articleTitle: Quantum memories and large-scale quantum coherence based on Raman interactions
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Applied research into quantum technologies and fundamental research into the foundations of quantum mechanics run hand in hand, since our understanding of quantum correlations both advances, and is advanced by, our ability to control large quantum systems. The off-resonant Raman interaction of light with material systems provides a powerful tool both for quantum information processing, and for accessing macroscopic non-classical states of matter. We describe a recent demonstration of entanglement between the motion of separated diamond crystals at room temperature, and the implementation of quantum memories in cesium vapour that can store and retrieve photons on demand with a time-bandwidth product exceeding 2000, both based on Raman scattering.

articleTitle: Magneto-optical nonreciprocal devices in silicon waveguides
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Optical nonreciprocal devices such as isolators and circulators play unique roles in photonic circuits. The optical nonreciprocal devices are discussed that are based on magneto-optical materials bonded on silicon waveguides.

articleTitle: Photonic crystal nanobeam cavities with an ultrahigh quality factor-to-modal volume ratio
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We describe the design, fabrication, and characterization of 1-dimensional silicon photonic crystal cavities with quality factor-to-modal volume ratios greater than 106 in which the maximum of the electric field is in air.

articleTitle: Experimental bosonsampling in a photonic circuit
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: The extended Church-Turing thesis posits that any computable function can be calculated efficiently by a probabilistic Turing machine. If this thesis held true, the global effort to build quantum computers might ultimately be unnecessary. The thesis would however be strongly contradicted by a physical device that efficiently performs a task believed to be intractable for classical computers. BosonSampling—the sampling from a distribution of n photons undergoing some linear-optical process—is a recently developed, and experimentally accessible example of such a task [1].

articleTitle: An all-silicon optical diode transmitting 10 Gbps data
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: An optical diode based on thermo-optic effect in silicon micro-resonators enables non-reciprocal transmission through direction dependent resonance shift. One-way 10Gbps data transmission is realized through the strong dispersion and attenuation associated with a resonant structure.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of EDFAs supporting 6 spatial modes
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Numerical and experimental studies of few-modes Erbium-doped fibers amplifiers suitable for mode-division multiplexing are presented. Based on simulations, fiber with tailored Erbium spatial distribution has been designed to support and amplify 6 spatial modes. Realizations are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Scalable and modular high-performance optical interconnects with distributed control plane
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We will discuss architectures, technologies, and benchmarking of massively parallel interconnections made possible by AWGR based switches with distributed control plane. Successful testbed experiments and silicon photonic chip implementations will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Inducing electro-optic photonic transitions for enabling isolation in silicon photonics
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We show approaches for achieving CMOS compatible on-chip isolators. The devices are achieved by inducing photonic GHz electro-optic transitions on a time scale faster than the photon time of flight in the structure.

articleTitle: Green, smart optical packet switching network with flow control for data centers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Hybrid optoelectronic packet routers with 100Gbps (25Gbps × 4 wavelengths) links are introduced in an intra-DC network. A novel “Express path” enables the flow control to reduce the latency and the power consumption.

articleTitle: Semiconductor membrane photonic devices for ultra-low power consumption operation
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Our research activities of GaInAsP/InP lateral current injection semiconductor membrane lasers and related devices intended for on-chip optical interconnects are reviewed and remaining issues to be solved for ultra-low power consumption operation are discussed.

articleTitle: Magnetophotonics and their applications in hologram memory and 3D display
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Introduction of nano-scaled artificial structures into magnetic materials provides us a variety of opportunities for controlling light traveling in the media. Magnetophotonic crystals (MPCs)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1, 2</sup> are classified into such materials, where optical-order periodic structures composed of magnetic and/or dielectric materials are introduced so as to create photonic band gap and to confine light in the vicinity of additional defects in the periodic structures. From one-dimensional (1D) (Fig.1) to 3-dimensional (3D) MPCs have been constructed actually, and among them, 1D or 2D artificial structures have been used and discussed in electronic and optical applications.

articleTitle: Generation of photon pairs, triplets, and non-diffracting single photons
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We discuss the generation of non-classical light with optimized properties including photon pairs ranging from factorable to highly entangled, photon triplets and non-diffracting heralded single photons. We will focus mainly on the last of these topics.

articleTitle: Overcoming SiN film stress limitations for high quality factor ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We overcome stress limitations of thick SiN films using termination trenches to isolate the device area from crack propagation. We measure an unprecedented quality factor of 6.5 million in a high confinement SiN ring resonator.

articleTitle: Quantum statistical testing of a QRNG algorithm
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We present the algorithmic design of a quantum random number generator, the subsequent synthesis of a physical design and its verification using quantum statistical testing. We also describe how quantum statistical testing can be used to diagnose channel noise in QKD protocols.

articleTitle: Surface-normal electro-aborption MQW modulator-based chip-scale optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: A MQW/EAM-based chip-scale photonic interconnect concept, that uses efficient CW VCSELs as sources and a lithographically-defined high-density multi-mode waveguide fabric, is analyzed. Projected energy-per-bit, bandwidth density, and packaging tolerances enable scaling with foreseeable CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Separating arbitrary overlapping spatial modes losslessly and without calculations
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We show how to separate arbitrary orthogonal spatial modes in an approach that avoids fundamental splitting loss, requires no calculations, compensates for drift in components or beams, and could be implemented with silicon photonics.

articleTitle: Orbital angular momentum states for mode division multiplexing in optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Orbital angular momentum states offer a potential path to mode division multiplexing in optical fiber. We review progress on a new class of fibers that support stable propagation of these states.

articleTitle: Experimental study of elementary inter-modal nonlinear interactions in a long few-mode fiber
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We report the results of an experimental investigation of inter-modal nonlinearities in a 4.7-km few-mode fiber (FMF). Both inter-modal cross-phase modulation (IM-XPM) and inter-modal four-wave mixing (IM-FWM) have been observed between waves separated by a several Terahertz.

articleTitle: Recent progress in metallic cavity nanolasers of subwavelength sizes
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: This talk will review the most recent progress on metallic cavity nanolasers with sub-wavelength size cavities, especially the efforts towards the first demonstration of CW operation at room temperature under electrical injection.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional coherently coupled vertical cavity laser arrays
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: The work has demonstrated both top and bottom emitting coherently coupled VCSEL arrays operating in the preferred in-phase supermode. Moreover, it was shown that phase tuning between the array elements is possible with varying injection current to the array elements. With the bottom emitting arrays, these would be able to scale up the array size, maximum power, and beam steering properties.

articleTitle: Advanced substrate-independent VCSELs
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We have transferred epitaxial layers between wafers and we have fabricated VCSELs on new host substrates. This procedure facilitates more advanced VCSEL designs by providing processing access to both sides of the epitaxial layers.

articleTitle: Semiconductor quantum well lasers with nanoscale resonant periodic active layers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Quantum dot semiconductor lasers have been the subject of significant investigation for many years. In part this is for potential applications based on desirable properties when compared with traditional quantum well-based lasers such as ultra-low threshold current density and reduced temperature sensitivity [1]. The most common technique for quantum dot growth is the self-assembly technique, in which dots form as a result of the large strain which exists between the dot material and substrate material. Unfortunately self-assembly results in dots with random positions and a broad size distribution. This leads to inhomogeneous broadening, decreased peak gain, and increased threshold current density. The lack of complete control over individual quantum dot properties inherent with the self-assembly technique has been the predominant obstacle to realizing their full potential for use in photonic devices.

articleTitle: Demonstration of low-noise phase-sensitive amplification and multicasting
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We review the recent advances in ultra-low noise optical amplification and frequency multicasting relying on two-and four-mode parametric phase-sensitive processes, respectively. Their potential applications in future optical communications and real-time signal processing are discussed.

articleTitle: The QKD network: From metropolitan to wide area
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Secure communication and information protection become more and more important in the modern society. Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables two remote legitimate users to share unconditionally secure keys. Different from the former ones, the security of these keys is based on the principles of quantum physics and could be proved. Combined with one-time pad encryption, QKD can provide us an effective way for secure communication and information protection <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1, 2]</sup>. Since Bennett and Brassard proposed the famous BB84 protocol <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</sup>, QKD or quantum cryptography has become one of the most dynamic research fields. After about twenty years of development, experimental QKD has achieved significant improvements, such as the transmission distance increased from 32 cm <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[4]</sup> to 260 km <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[5]</sup>, the speed increased from 200 Hz <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[4]</sup> to 10 GHz <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[6]</sup>.

articleTitle: Research programs in photonics at NSF
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: The National Science Foundation (NSF) is an independent federal agency created by Congress in 1950 “to promote the progress of science; to advance the national health, prosperity, and welfare; to secure the national defense...” With an annual budget of about $7.0 billion (FY 2012), NSF is the funding source for approximately 20 percent of all federally supported basic research conducted by America's colleges and universities.

articleTitle: Laterally-coupled-cavity VCSELs for push-pull high speed modulation
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Laterally-coupled-cavity VCSELs using bow-tie shape oxide aperture is demonstrated. The lasing characteristics show clear evidence of coherent lateral coupling. High-speed push-pull-modulation free from relaxation oscillation frequency is expected via spatially altering the transverse mode distribution.

articleTitle: Linear and passive silicon diodes, isolators, and logic gates
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Silicon photonic integrated devices and circuits have offered a promising means to revolutionalize information processing and computing technologies. In this talk we present our recent efforts of design, fabrication, and characterization of ultracompact, linear, passive on-chip optical diodes, isolators and logic gates based on silicon two-dimensional photonic crystal slabs. Both simulation and experiment results show high performance of these novel designed devices. The success of these devices would help to construct nanophotonic on-chip processor architectures for future optical computers.

articleTitle: Demonstration of nonorthogonal multi-state discrimination below the standard quantum limit
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We demonstrate the discrimination of four nonorthogonal states below the standard quantum limit (SQL) for a wide range of input powers, and achieving error probabilities four times lower than the SQL.

articleTitle: Rolled-up 1.5 µm InAs quantum dot tube lasers and integrated nanophotonic circuits on Si
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Low threshold, ultrahigh speed micro- and nanoscale lasers that can be directly integrated with optoelectronic and electronic components on a CMOS chip are in demand for future chip-level optical communications. In this regard, rolled-up semiconductor tube optical cavities, formed when coherently strained nanomembranes are selectively released from the host substrate, have emerged as a promising approach to realize high performance lasers on Si. <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1–3</sup> We have investigated the design, fabrication, and characterization of InAs/InGaAsP quantum dot tube lasers. We report the first demonstration of semiconductor tube lasers that can operate at the telecom wavelength (∼ 1.5 µm). Such devices can exhibit an extremely low threshold (∼ 1.26 µW) and multiple emission wavelengths. The direct integration of quantum dot tube devices with Si waveguides has also been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Etchless optical cavity using metal nanowires on dielectric-metal slab waveguide
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We demonstrate that randomly distributed metallic nanowires on the dielectric-metal slab waveguides can form Fabry-Perot-type optical cavities and achieve sufficient quality factors for lasing for the transverse electric waveguide mode.

articleTitle: Long photon lifetime from microdisk cavity laser with type II GaSb/GaAs quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Microdisk lasers with active region made of type II GaSb/GaAs quantum dots on the GaAs substrate have been demonstrated. Lasing wavelengths near 1μm was achieved and longer photon lifetime from type II structure also observed.

articleTitle: Ultra high optical nonreciprocity using silicon microring resonators
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: An ultra high nonreciprocal transmission ratio of 40 dB is achieved using an all-silicon optical diode. By experimentally studying the power dynamics of individual microring resonators, we investigate the device mechanism and offer improvements.

articleTitle: Electrically controlled photonic crystal nanocavity sources and modulators
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We report recent advances in electrically controlled photonic crystal nanocavity light sources and modulators, including an electrically pumped laser with 181nA threshold, an ultrafast single-mode LED with sub-fJ/bit operation energy, and modulator with 0.2 fJ/bit modulation energy. Additionally, we model the electrical and thermal performance of the lateral p-i-n geometry utilized in these devices, determining design criteria for efficient electrical injection and finding minimal self-heating.

articleTitle: A proposal of coupled resonator optical waveguides based on slotted nanobeam cavities
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We propose coupled resonator optical waveguides based on slotted nanobeam cavities. Numerical results show that our proposed structure can achieve a high effective nonlinear coefficient because of small group velocity and small effective mode area.

articleTitle: Quantum communication with ultrafast multimode pulsed light
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Using ultrafast multimode PDC sources and optical quantum pulse gates based on engineered frequency conversion processes we introduce multiplexed quantum information coding and show that it enables an exponential increase in the achievable quantum communication rate.

articleTitle: Low-noise frequency downconversion for long-distance distribution of entangled atomic qubits
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Distribution of quantum resources such as entanglement over distances beyond a few fiber attenuation lengths requires realization of quantum repeaters that utilize entanglement swapping to extend the distance between the entangled qubit pairs [1]. A quantum repeater is a small quantum computer capable of generating entangled qubit pairs with its neighboring repeaters and storing them in stable quantum memories. Once the entangled pairs are generated, it will perform Bell basis measurements, classical communication with appropriate repeaters, and single qubit gates necessary for entanglement swapping. For high fidelity operation, it might perform local operations and classical communications (LOCC) such as entanglement distillation [2] and/or quantum error correction [3,4]. Generation of remote entangled ion pairs mediated by photonic qubits has been demonstrated [5] but their reach is limited since the photons used in the experiment are in the UV part of the spectrum. Coherent conversion of the photons emitted by Yb ion at 369.5nm to a photon at 1310 nm would enable entanglement generation over long distances [6].

articleTitle: “Phonon diodes” and reciprocity in reflection and transmission
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Recent years have seen increased interest in acoustic “diodes” or “rectifiers”. Surprisingly, many of the proposed designs of these devices are based on passive linear structures without magnetic fields that ought to be perfectly reciprocal. Furthermore, it has been suggested that ballistic phonon transport through such structures can yield “thermal diodes”. In this didactical presentation, acoustic “diodes” will be discussed in the broader context of reciprocity in reflection/transmission (R-T) of waves. We will review a theorem known in optoelectronics but under-appreciated in acoustics and phonon physics, stating that the matrix of R-T coefficients for properly normalized amplitudes is symmetric for linear systems that conform to power conservation and time reversibility for wave fields. The power of this theorem is in that it is valid for waves of any nature and not limited to systems described by a particular set of equations, be it acoustics or electromagnetism. We will show how this theorem applies to various wave phenomena, including inter-conversion of electromagnetic and acoustic waves in piezoelectric structures, and discuss a conjecture that R-T reciprocity is preserved in the presence of linear dissipation. We will see that linear structures hitherto proposed for acoustic “diodes” in fact do obey R-T reciprocity, and thus do not yield true isolators. In order to create a linear isolator one needs to break the time-reversal symmetry either by using a magnetic field or by actively modulating the parameters of the device. In acoustics, both paths can be pursued but neither has been explored so far. We will also review studies of nonlinear acoustic “diodes” and conclude that those, likewise, failed so far to demonstrate an acoustic isolator. Finally, we will consider the relationship between acoustic isolators and “thermal diodes”, and show that ballistic phonon transport through a linear structure, whether an acoustic isolator or not, is unlikely to form the basis for a thermal diode. This contribution was supported as part of the S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>TEC Energy Frontier Research Center funded by the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Basic Energy Sciences under Award No. DE-SC0001299.

articleTitle: End-to-end demonstration of optical multicasting over a dynamically-reconfigurable hybrid data center network architecture
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: A hybrid data center network architecture featuring reconfigurable optical functionalities is presented and evaluated on an end-to-end test bed. Physical layer multicast is successfully verified via video streaming and UDP performance measurements.

articleTitle: Ge/SiGe quantum well asymmetric Fabry-Perot modulators on silicon substrates
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We demonstrate vertical-incidence Ge/SiGe quantum well modulators, fabricated directly on silicon, for free-space chip-to-chip optical interconnects. The devices exhibit greater than 10 dB extinction ratio, low insertion loss, and 2 Gb/s operation.

articleTitle: Artificial faraday rotation using active metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We demonstrate microwave gyrotropic metamaterials without an external magnetic bias, by translating the property of unidirectional active electronic circuits into effective dielectric response. Strong bulk Faraday effects were observed in both simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Optical interconnect technologies enabling high-performance servers
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: High-speed and compact optical interconnect is indispensable to realize high-performance servers. We developed compact optical transceiver and optical mid-plane with high-density connectors and wiring. Using them, 1500-optical-connections and 37.5 Tb/s-bandwidth in a server were achieved.

articleTitle: One-way effects in magnetoplasmonic and -photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: By judiciously combining symmetries in magnetooptic systems with PhC resonances strong unidirectional band gaps can be created. This allows for ultracompact one-way mirrors and deflectors. Magnetoplasmonic extraordinary transmission systems can likewise be made strongly unidirectional by combining slit resonances with SPP resonances.

articleTitle: Hybrid integration of laser diode and magneto-optic waveguides based on adhesive bonding
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Adhesive bonding for integrating a laser diode and an optical isolator was investigated. The coupling efficiency was calculated by beam propagation method and experimental results of adhesive bonding were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous integrated systems for future computing and networking
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We will discuss throughput, power, latency, and parallelism needs in computing and networking systems that drive micro/nano-scale integration of various processing, storage, and interconnection components. Heterogeneous integrated systems will be covered in detail.

articleTitle: Nanopatch cavity with a subwavelength-scale cuboidal semiconductor core
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We propose a modified nanopatch cavity with a cuboidal semiconductor sandwiched between extended metal planes. Experimental results show the quality factor of ~200 can be achieved with an effective mode volume of ~0.0064 cubic wavelength.

articleTitle: Mode group demultiplexing and modal dispersion compensation using spatial-spectral holography
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Spatial-spectral holographic signal processing is used for modal-dispersion compensation to enable wideband mode-group multiplexing and demultiplexing in transparent spatially-multiplexed multi-mode fiber networks with an unprecedented aggregate bandwidth and routing and switching capabilities.

articleTitle: Metallic wall-based plasmon nanocavities with 1-D photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We propose a metallic wall-based plasmon nanocavity with 1-D photonic crystals. Numerical results show that the proposed structure achieves a mode volume of 0.39(λ/n)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and a Q factor of 604.

articleTitle: Thermal nanoimprint fabrication of chalcogenide glass waveguide resonators on nonconventional plastic substrates
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We demonstrated thermal nanoimprint fabrication of photonic devices in chalcogenide glass films on both semiconductor and nonconventional plastic substrates. A high micro-ring intrinsic quality factor of 3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> is achieved at 1550 nm wavelength.

articleTitle: Site-controlled QDs: A route for dense arrays of integrated entangled photon emitters
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Quantum computing is one of future challenges [1]. One of the technologies baring significant potentialities is based on quantum dots (QD), usually referred to as “artificial atoms”. The analogy refers to their discrete energy levels, which allows atomic concepts to be exported to a system which is, on the other hand, embedded in a semiconductor matrix and can be technologically exploited. A good example of this is the capability to emit single and polarization-entangled photons [2], which are attractive sources of qubits. However, many challenges still have to be overcome. The main problem of most of QD systems is the asymmetry induced fine-structure splitting (FSS) - the degeneracy lifting of the exciton (e+h) level. It compromises entanglement detection which, in general, resides in the polarization of photons emitted in biexciton (2e+2h)-exciton recombination cascade (note: the entanglement resides in the electronic levels, not in the cascaded process). Particular tuning strategies (magnetic field, electric field, strain), indeed, can rectify this issue, however they complicate the set-up and typically can be applied to a single QD at a time, while an array of symmetrical QDs is needed for complicated quantum computational tasks.

articleTitle: Metal-cavity quantum-dot surface-emitting microlaser: Theory and experiment
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We report our recent experimental and theoretical development on metal-cavity surface-emitting quantum-dot microlasers. Room-temperature operation is achieved for devices with diameters close to one wavelength. The experimental data agrees well with our developed theoretical model.

articleTitle: Recent advances in photonic bandgap fiber technology
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We review our recent progress in the fabrication, characterization, modeling and splicing of wide transmission bandwidth hollow core photonic bandgap fibers and discuss their modal properties and potential for data transmission.

articleTitle: A first glance at coherent optical transmission using photonic bandgap fiber as a transmission medium
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Photonic bandgap fibers (PBGF) potentially offer a very substantial increase of capacity per fiber over solid core fibers. We review transmission experiments using PBGF and their viability for next-generation transmissions systems.

articleTitle: Ultra-large-capacity multi-core fiber transmission technologies
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: The paper reviews recent works on and issues with ultra-large-capacity transmission based on multi-core space-division-multiplexing. 1Pbs multi-core fiber transmission based on space-division-multiplexing and multi-level modulation/demodulation is also introduced.

articleTitle: CMOS compatible photonic crystal VCSELs: A wealth of new photonic functionality
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: CMOS-compatible III–V/Si vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) based on a double set of photonic crystal reflectors are demonstrated, showing single-mode continuous-wave operation at 1.55-µm with thresholds in the sub-mW range. The natural propensity of these VCSEL devices for achieving a wide range of functionality is discussed.

articleTitle: Entropy power inequalities and classical capacities of bosonic noise channels
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Characterizing information-carrying capacities of bosonic communication channels is of significant practical interest. For thermal noise channels, using coherent (product) states yields an achievable rate for classical communication which is conjectured to be optimal. However, it is not known whether coding strategies using entanglement may perform better. Here we discuss upper bounds on classical capacities of thermal noise channels. These imply that coherent-state coding is close to optimal. Our main tool is a quantum analog of the entropy power inequality introduced Shannon. It gives a lower bound on the output von Neumann entropy when two independent signals combine at a beamsplitter.

articleTitle: Electrically-pumped membrane-reflector surface-emitters on silicon
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We report here electrically-pumped membrane reflector surface-emitters on silicon based on transferred InGaAsP QW structures sandwiched in between two single-layer Fano resonance photonic crystal membrane reflectors on silicon substrate.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal and unidirectional optical bloch oscillations
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Nonreciprocal optical Bloch oscillations are shown to suppress optical beam revival in one propagation direction in asymmetric waveguide arrays. Their application to optical isolation is predicted to yield isolation ratios as large as 55 dB.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of EDFAs supporting 6 spatial modes
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Numerical and experimental studies of few-modes Erbium-doped fibers amplifiers suitable for mode-division multiplexing are presented. Based on simulations, fiber with tailored Erbium spatial distribution has been designed to support and amplify 6 spatial modes. Realizations are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Mode selectivity with quantum-state-preserving frequency conversion using four-wave mixing
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We consider quantum frequency conversion using four-wave mixing Bragg scattering and the prospects for multiplexing using the temporal modes.We find that there is an optimal strength parameter, but that the fiber length is less critical.

articleTitle: Taming the flow of light via Parity-Time Symmetry
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We introduce the notion of Parity-Time Symmetry (PTS) and present its implications in wave transport. Using photonics and electronics frameworks we propose designs that support asymmetric transport due to the interplay of PTS and nonlinearity.

articleTitle: Phase-sensitive noiseless amplification and frequency conversion of spatially-multimode light
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: We discuss the recent insights into the spatial-mode structure of traveling-wave optical parametric amplifiers, with focus on optical processing of quantum images.

articleTitle: Optimal partitioned-interval detection binary quantum receiver with practical devices
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: Partitioned-interval detection binary quantum receiver with non-ideal devices is theoretically analysed. Using global optimized partition strategy, relatively large gain over standard quantum limit (SQL) is obtained with small partition number for certain mean photon number.

articleTitle: Aloha
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Photonics Society Summer Topical Meeting Series
abstract: On behalf of the IEEE Photonics Society, I want like to welcome you to the 2013 Summer Topical Meetings held on the beautiful Big Island of Hawaii. With more than 20 years of tradition, the IEEE Summer Topicals are the premier conferences for emerging fields in photonic science, device technologies, and applications. The conferences are held to create the opportunity to learn about exciting new topics and to interact with the research and technology leaders in an intimate environment. This year the Topical Meetings are: •Micro- and Nano-Cavity Integrated Photonics •Space-Division Multiplexing for Optical Communication •Quantum Photonics & Communications •Non-Reciprocal Photonic Devices •Data Center Photonics
